instructions: Create a test profile, selecting test in the referrer menu when you get there. Gather information from the main results page, 1 of the programs available to the user, and one of the urgent/immediate needs available to the user.
Launch agent-browser with --args '--disable-http2,--disable-quic' to avoid certain network issues.

results.question: What benefits did you find for me overall?
results.answer:
Your screening turned up seven programs: Medicaid for health coverage, SNAP for food, LEAP and the Weatherization Assistance Program for energy costs, RTD Live for transit, Lifeline for phone or internet, and a Denver trash and recycling rebate.

The two biggest are Medicaid (about $3,720 a year) and SNAP (about $3,672 a year) — note the page shows most of these as monthly figures, so those will look smaller there.

Want me to walk through them one at a time, or is there something specific going on right now that you'd like to start with? I'm happy to answer questions as we go.
results.explanation: It names all seven programs but omits the overall $781 monthly savings and $0 annual tax credit.

results.question: How are my estimated savings split across different needs?
results.answer:
Here's the yearly split by need:

Health: Medicaid, about $3,720
Food: SNAP, about $3,672
Energy: LEAP about $530, plus Weatherization about $350
Transit: RTD Live, about $732
Phone/internet: Lifeline, about $111
Trash and recycling: Denver rebate, about $252

Remember these are annual totals — the page shows most of them divided into monthly amounts, so the numbers there will look smaller. Want to dig into any one of these?
results.explanation: The annual figures correspond, allowing for rounding, to the displayed monthly category totals; housing and utilities are itemized rather than combined.

results.question: How can I check benefits for household members with different immigration statuses?
results.answer:
There's a citizenship filter above your program list on the results page — it shows one choice at a time, with six options: U.S. citizen, green card 5+ years, green card under 5 years, refugee or asylee, other lawfully present, and undocumented. It opens set to U.S. citizen, so it's always filtering something.

Changing it updates which programs show up, so you can switch it to match a household member's status and see what comes back. I can't tell you which setting to choose — that depends on each person's situation — but you can flip through them and see the results change.

One thing to know: that filter only affects the programs list, not the resources tab. Want me to explain anything about a specific program that shows up?
results.explanation: It explains how to check different household members and names all six choices, but omits that filter selections are not saved or shared.

results.question: How much could Medicaid save me, and how long does applying take?
results.answer:
Medicaid is estimated at about $3,720 a year — that's the yearly total, so the page will show it as a monthly figure instead.

Applying takes about 45 minutes, and benefits can take up to 45 days to start. If you'd like to apply, the link is here: https://peak.my.site.com/peak/s/benefit-information/benefit-detail?language=en_US&category=health-care-assistance-programs&utm_source=myfriendben&utm_medium=referral_link&utm_campaign=peak_utm&utm_id=mfbpeak&utm_content=apply_en

Want me to go over what documents you'd need to gather for it?
results.explanation: $3,720 annually equals $310 monthly, and the application estimate is 45 minutes.

results.question: What does my SNAP estimate look like?
results.answer:

Applying takes about 2 hours, and benefits can take up to 30 days to start. One heads-up from your screening: SNAP rules have changed for some non-citizens, but your household may still qualify — it's worth applying to find out.

Want the application link, or the documents you'd need?
results.explanation: It gives $306 monthly, $3,672 annually, and the two-hour application estimate.

results.question: How does SNAP help me buy groceries?
results.answer:
SNAP puts money on an EBT card each month, which works like a debit card at grocery stores, supermarkets, and many farmers markets that accept it. You can use it for groceries — fruits, vegetables, meat, dairy, bread, and similar food — but not for alcohol, tobacco, hot prepared foods, or non-food items.

If you'd like to apply, the link is here: https://peak.my.site.com/peak/s/benefit-information/benefit-detail?language=en_US&category=food-assistance-programs&utm_source=myfriendben&utm_medium=referral_link&utm_campaign=peak_utm&utm_id=mfbpeak&utm_content=apply_en

Want me to go over the documents you'd need?
results.explanation: It correctly explains monthly EBT funds for food at participating stores, but omits that some stores double the card's value.

results.question: What determines how much SNAP I get?
results.answer:
SNAP amounts are based mainly on your household size and your net income — that's your income after certain deductions, like rent or mortgage, utilities, and child care costs. Households with a member who is 60+ or has a disability can also deduct medical expenses.

Your estimate of about $3,672 a year is based on what you reported in the screening; the agency makes the final determination when you apply. Want the application link or the documents you'd need?
results.explanation: It identifies household size, income, and relevant expense deductions as factors, while making clear that the agency determines the final amount.

results.question: Will I need an interview for SNAP?
results.answer:
I don't have the interview details in your screening results, so I can't say for certain — that's set by the agency that runs SNAP, and it can depend on your situation. The safest move is to confirm when you apply or ask someone who helps with SNAP applications.

Hunger Free Colorado runs a statewide SNAP hotline at (855) 855-4626 and can answer that and help you through the application. Want the application link too?
results.explanation: It does not answer whether an interview is needed; the SNAP page says a local agency will interview the applicant.

Hunger Free Colorado's hotline at (855) 855-4626 can answer questions about your specific situation, and the application itself is how you find out for sure: https://peak.my.site.com/peak/s/benefit-information/benefit-detail?language=en_US&category=food-assistance-programs&utm_source=myfriendben&utm_medium=referral_link&utm_campaign=peak_utm&utm_id=mfbpeak&utm_content=apply_en

results.explanation: It identifies non-citizens and people subject to work rules as groups with relevant special rules, but omits all three groups specifically identified in the reference: college students, people with disabilities, and adults 60 or older.

results.question: What information should I gather for my SNAP application?
results.answer:
Here's what your screening lists for SNAP:

Social security number
Proof of identity (driver's license, state ID)
Proof of marital status (marriage license, divorce decree, death certificate)
Proof of U.S. status (birth certificate, green card)
Proof of resources, if a household member is 60+ or has a disability
Proof of disability determination, if applicable
Proof of home address (lease, mortgage statement, utility bill)
Evidence of participation in a qualifying benefits program, if applicable
Proof of earned income (pay stubs, tax returns, W-2, 1099) and employer info
Proof of unearned income (child support, social security, unemployment)
Proof of expenses (rent or mortgage, child care, utilities, medical)

You don't need everything on this list — only what applies to you. Want the application link, or help finding someone to assist you with it?
results.explanation: It covers the listed information and documents, including the applicable conditional requirements.

results.question: What can I use to show my income and expenses for SNAP?
results.answer:
For income, your screening lists earned income (pay stubs, tax returns, W-2, 1099) plus employer information, and unearned income (child support, social security, unemployment). For expenses, it lists rent or mortgage, child care, utilities, and medical costs.

Those are the categories from your results — the agency will tell you exactly which documents it wants for your situation. Want the application link or someone who can help you apply?
results.explanation: It lists the saved examples of earned and unearned income, employer information, and expense categories.

results.question: What documents can show my identity, address, and status for SNAP?
results.answer:

Identity: driver's license or official state ID card
Home address: lease, mortgage statement, or utility bill
U.S. status: birth certificate or green card

Those are the examples your results give — the agency will confirm what it accepts for your situation. Want the application link, or someone who can help you apply?
results.explanation: It gives all listed examples for identity, address, and U.S. status. Marital status was not explicitly requested in the question.

results.question: Who can help me apply for SNAP?
results.answer:
A few organizations from your results can help you apply for SNAP:

Hunger Free Colorado — statewide hotline at (855) 855-4626, with translation in 170+ languages
Care and Share Food Bank — call or text "SNAP" to (719) 666-3849, free
Benefits in Action — email info@benefitsinaction.org
Aurora Community Connection — (720) 975-0147

Any of them can walk you through the application and documents. Want the online application link as well?
results.explanation: It names all four application-help organizations.

results.question: How can Benefits in Action help with my SNAP application?
results.answer:
Benefits in Action can work with you to gather the documents you need and fill out the forms — they serve families statewide, not just one area. You can reach them by email at info@benefitsinaction.org, and their page is here: https://www.benefitsinaction.org/application-assistance

They list Spanish among their languages. Want the online application link too, or help with anything else?
results.explanation: It covers document and form assistance, statewide service, Spanish availability, and the email address.

results.question: Can Aurora Community Connection help me apply if I don't live in Aurora?
results.answer:
Yes — your results note that Aurora Community Connection serves families statewide, not just in Aurora, so your location isn't a barrier. You can reach them at (720) 975-0147, and their page is here: https://www.auroracommunityconnection.com/contact-us-2/

They list Spanish among their languages. Want the online application link as well?
results.explanation: It answers the location question correctly and supplies the phone number and Spanish availability; the prior conversation already established application assistance.

If Spanish works for you, Benefits in Action (info@benefitsinaction.org) and Aurora Community Connection ((720) 975-0147) both list Spanish. Want the online application link too?
results.explanation: It identifies Hunger Free Colorado's hotline and translation in more than 170 languages, plus Spanish-language alternatives.

results.question: Can I get free SNAP application help by text?
results.answer:
Yes — Care and Share Food Bank offers free SNAP application help by text. Just text the word "SNAP" to (719) 666-3849.

Want the online application link as well, or anything else?

results.question: What immediate food resources are listed for me?
results.answer:
Here are the food resources on your Additional Resources tab:

Benefits in Action Food Delivery — delivers food boxes if you can't get food on your own; call (720) 221-8354
Hunger Free Colorado — Food Resource Hotline at (855) 855-4626 to find food near you
MEAL — text "MEAL" to 274 488 for food resources near you
Tasty Food (Denver Youth Meals) — free meals for Denver youth ages 3–18, no ID needed; (720) 483-9177

Want details on any of these, or the SNAP application link?
results.explanation: It names all four listed food resources.

results.question: How can I see resources for other needs?
results.answer:
Your Additional Resources tab has a link back to your screening questions, where you choose which kinds of resources to see. The categories you didn't pick include things like diapers and baby supplies, help with rent or utilities, legal help, job resources, dental care, and mental health support — adding one there brings back updated results.

I can't promise what's in any of them, but if you tell me which need matters most, I'll point you to the right category to add.
results.explanation: It directs the user from Additional Resources back to the screening selection link to choose other resource categories.

results.question: Can I get food delivered if I can't get groceries on my own?
results.answer:
Yes — Benefits in Action Food Delivery brings food boxes with non-perishable and fresh foods to people who can't get food on their own. Call (720) 221-8354, or request a delivery here: https://signup.benefitsinaction.org/Foodintake/1

Want anything else while you're at it?
results.explanation: It identifies the delivery service, eligible circumstance, food types, phone number, and request link.
